title: Decisions: if and switch
bridge: Java's `if` puts the condition in **brackets** and the block in **braces**: `if (kg > 100) { ... } else if (kg > 0) { ... } else { ... }`. "And" is `&&`, "or" is `||`, "not" is `!`. Java also has `switch` for choosing among fixed values.

notes: if / else if / else in a method.
switch with arrows returns a value.

exercises.title: Grades
exercises.prompt: Write grade(int score): 80+ "A", 65+ "B", 50+ "C", 40+ "D", below 40 "E", and "invalid" if below 0 or above 100.
hints: Check invalid first: if (score < 0 || score > 100) return "invalid";
Then from the top grade down.

exercises.title: Leap years
exercises.prompt: Write isLeap(int year): divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100 aren't, except years divisible by 400 are.

exercises.title: Day names with switch
exercises.prompt: Write dayName(int n) using a switch: 1 is "Monday" … 7 is "Sunday", anything else "?".

tests.why: Use a switch for this one.

quiz.why: && (the single & is a different, bitwise operator).

quiz.q: What does x > 5 ? "yes" : "no" give when x is 3?
quiz.why: The ternary picks the second value when the condition is false.

quiz.q: Why always use braces even for one line?
choices: Adding a second line later silently falls outside the if
quiz.why: Without braces, only the first line belongs to the if.

explain: Explain decisions: if and switch to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
